record.what_it_does: Zendesk is a customer service/helpdesk platform for managing support tickets, help center content, live chat, voice, and omnichannel customer conversations.
record.auth_notes: Zendesk documents OAuth access tokens (Bearer, via OAuth2 authorization flows) as the primary/recommended method, and API tokens sent via HTTP Basic auth as a deprecated alternative. A single-account 'local' OAuth client can be self-created in Admin Center, but an app that serves multiple Zendesk customers must use a 'global OAuth client', which only Zendesk can create/convert after reviewing a request — developers cannot generate global OAuth clients themselves.
record.access_notes: Developers can self-serve a working Zendesk instance via a 14-day free trial (no credit card required) and create a local OAuth client or API token immediately. However, ongoing production use requires a paid plan (from $19/agent/month), and any agent toolkit meant to serve multiple end customers additionally needs a Zendesk-approved 'global OAuth client', gating true multi-tenant distribution behind vendor approval.
record.main_blocker: Multi-tenant distribution requires a Zendesk-approved 'global OAuth client' (self-serve local OAuth clients only work for single-account/internal use), and production use requires a paid plan after the 14-day trial.

record.open_questions: Zendesk's own support docs mention Zendesk can 'act as an MCP server' exposing tools to third-party AI agents, but no public endpoint, docs page, or URL for this is published/discoverable — it appears to be an in-product/EAP capability rather than a documented external MCP server, so it was not counted as 'official' MCP. Worth re-checking developer.zendesk.com for a dedicated MCP server doc page if this becomes GA.
